title: BEYOND STRUCTURE: INVARIANT CRYSTAL PROPERTY PREDICTION WITH PSEUDO-PARTICLE RAY DIFFRACTION
research_summary: Crystal property prediction, governed by quantum mechanical principles, is computationally prohibitive to solve exactly for large many-body systems using traditional density functional theory. While machine learning models have emerged as efficient approximations for large-scale applications, their performance is strongly influenced by the choice of atomic representation. Although modern graph-based approaches have progressively incorporated more structural information, they often fail to capture long-range atomic interactions due to finite receptive fields and local encoding schemes. This limitation leads to distinct crystals being mapped to identical representations, hindering accurate property prediction. To address this, we introduce PRDNet that leverages unique reciprocal-space diffraction besides graph representations. To enhance sensitivity to elemental and environmental variations, we employ a data-driven pseudo-particle to generate a synthetic diffraction pattern. PRDNet ensures full invariance to crystallographic symmetries. Extensive experiments are conducted on Materials Project, JARVIS-DFT, and MatBench, demonstrating that the proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance.

title: A SINGLE ARCHITECTURE FOR REPRESENTING INVARIANCE UNDER ANY SPACE GROUP
research_summary: This paper introduces the Crystal Fourier Transformer (CFT), a single neural architecture that adapts its weights to enforce exact invariance to any of the 230 crystallographic space groups. It achieves this by analytically deriving constraints that group operations impose on Fourier coefficients, constructing symmetry-adapted Fourier bases via a dual graph representation, and encoding these constraints into a group-conditional routing matrix (MG) within a Transformer. The model is validated on material property prediction and zero-shot generalization to unseen space groups.

title: Accurate prediction of tensorial spectra using equivariant graph neural network
research_summary: This paper introduces the Tensorial Spectra Equivariant Neural Network (TSENN), an equivariant graph neural network that maps crystal structures directly to their full photon-frequency-dependent optical tensors—specifically, the complex dielectric tensor εαβ(ω) = εαβ₁(ω) + iεαβ₂—trained on frequency-dependent dielectric tensors of 1,432 bulk semiconductors. The model encodes isotropic (ℓ=0) and anisotropic (ℓ=2) sequential tensor components into spherical tensor representations to ensure symmetry-aware predictions consistent with crystalline symmetry constraints, achieving a mean absolute error of 0.127.

title: A framework to evaluate machine learning crystal stability predictions
research_summary: We present Matbench Discovery as an example evaluation framework for machine learning energy models, here applied as pre-filters to first-principles computed data in a high-throughput search for stable inorganic crystals.

title: Predicting thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds using ensemble machine learning based on electron configuration
research_summary: This paper proposes an ensemble machine learning framework—Electron Configuration models with Stacked Generalization (ECSG)—to predict the thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds. ECSG integrates three base-level models grounded in distinct domain knowledge: Magpie (atomic properties), Roost (interatomic interactions), and ECCNN (electron configuration). The framework uses stacked generalization to combine their outputs into a meta-level model, achieving high predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.988 on JARVIS) and exceptional sample efficiency (requiring only 1/7 the data of existing models). It is validated across multiple databases (MP, OQMD, JARVIS), applied to unknown composition spaces (perovskite halides, Li-containing oxides, transition metal oxides), and deployed in two case studies: discovery of 2D wide bandgap semiconductors and double perovskite oxides—both confirmed via first-principles DFT calculations.

title: Transformer-generated atomic embeddings to enhance prediction accuracy of crystal properties with machine learning
research_summary: This paper proposes a novel atomic embedding strategy called universal atomic embeddings (UAEs), generated via a custom Transformer-based model named CrystalTransformer (ct-UAEs), to improve the accuracy of machine learning predictions for crystal properties such as formation energy and bandgap. The ct-UAEs are pretrained on large crystal databases (MP*), transferred to various back-end GNN models (e.g., CGCNN, ALIGNN, MEGNET), and shown to yield consistent accuracy improvements (e.g., 14% MAE reduction for formation energy on MP). The embeddings demonstrate transferability across datasets (JARVIS, MC3D, HOIP) and tasks, interpretability via clustering (UMAP/K-means), and multi-task adaptability (MT@2p–MT@4p).

title: Accurate piezoelectric tensor prediction with equivariant attention tensor graph neural network
research_summary: The paper proposes an equivariant attention tensor graph neural network (EATGNN) to predict the full third-rank piezoelectric tensor for both bulk and 2D materials, leveraging irreducible representation decomposition to respect crystal symmetry and rotational equivariance. It validates predictions against DFT-calculated tensors, achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, and uses the model to screen and discover new high-performance piezoelectric candidates, subsequently confirmed by DFPT calculations.

title: Hierarchy-boosted funnel learning for identifying semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity
research_summary: The paper proposes a hierarchy-boosted funnel learning (HiBoFL) framework that integrates unsupervised and supervised learning to efficiently identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL), circumventing large-scale brute-force ab initio calculations. It uses unsupervised clustering on descriptors from the Materials Project database to narrow the search space, performs low-cost high-throughput calculations (PET model) on selected clusters to label κL, and trains an interpretable CatBoost classifier to predict ultralow κL, revealing new structural descriptors governing anharmonicity.

title: LLM-Prop: predicting the properties of crystalline materials using large language models
research_summary: This paper develops LLM-Prop, a method that leverages large language models (LLMs) to predict properties of crystalline materials from their text descriptions, outperforming state-of-the-art graph neural network (GNN)-based methods and domain-specific LLMs like MatBERT. It introduces the TextEdge benchmark dataset containing crystal text descriptions and their properties, and demonstrates that natural language input enables better capture of space group symmetry and Wyckoff sites than GNNs.

title: RETHINKING THE ROLE OF FRAMES FOR SE(3)-INVARIANT CRYSTAL STRUCTURE MODELING
research_summary: Crystal structure modeling with graph neural networks is essential for various applications in materials informatics, and capturing SE(3)-invariant geometric features is a fundamental requirement for these networks. A straightforward approach is to model with orientation-standardized structures through structure-aligned coordinate systems, or “frames.” However, unlike molecules, determining frames for crystal structures is challenging due to their infinite and highly symmetric nature. In particular, existing methods rely on a statically fixed frame for each structure, determined solely by its structural information, regardless of the task under consideration. Here, we rethink the role of frames, questioning whether such simplistic alignment with the structure is sufficient, and propose the concept of dynamic frames. While accommodating the infinite and symmetric nature of crystals, these frames provide each atom with a dynamic view of its local environment, focusing on actively interacting atoms. We demonstrate this concept by utilizing the attention mechanism in a recent transformer-based crystal encoder, resulting in a new architecture called CrystalFramer. Extensive experiments show that CrystalFramer outperforms conventional frames and existing crystal encoders in various crystal property prediction tasks.

title: A Denoising Pre-training Framework for Accelerating Novel Material Discovery
research_summary: The paper introduces an unsupervised Denoising Pre-training Framework (DPF) for crystal structures to overcome the scarcity of labeled data in crystal property prediction. DPF pre-trains models on 380,743 unlabeled crystal structures by reconstructing masked atom types, perturbed atom positions, and perturbed lattice constants. The pre-trained models are then fine-tuned on downstream crystal property prediction tasks (e.g., formation energy, band gap, bulk moduli). Experiments show DPF improves prediction accuracy across multiple benchmarks compared to prior models.

title: PDDFormer: Pairwise Distance Distribution Graph Transformer for Crystal Material Property Prediction
research_summary: The paper introduces WPDDFormer and UPDDFormer—graph transformer models that integrate atom-weighted and unit-cell pairwise distance distribution (PDD) representations into multi-edge crystal graphs—to achieve continuous and geometrically complete crystal structure representations for improved property prediction. It addresses discontinuity and ambiguity in traditional crystal graph representations caused by atomic vibrations and lattice non-uniqueness, and demonstrates state-of-the-art accuracy on Materials Project and JARVIS-DFT benchmarks.

title: Accelerating materials property prediction via a hybrid Transformer Graph framework that leverages four body interactions
research_summary: We propose a framework utilizing a Graph Neural Network with composition-based and crystal structure-based architectures, combined with a transfer learning scheme. This approach accurately predicts energy-related properties (e.g., total energy, energy above the convex hull, energy band gap) and data-scarce mechanical properties (e.g., bulk and shear modulus). Our model incorporates four-body interactions, capturing periodicity and structural characteristics. It outperforms state-of-the-art models in 8 materials property regression tasks.

title: Cross-scale covariance for material property prediction
research_summary: The paper proposes a statistical approach to predict large-scale material properties (specifically plastic flow strength in FCC metals) using regression on small-scale 'indicator' properties computed with the same interatomic potential (IP). It analyzes covariance between MD-simulated flow strength (QoI) and 39 small-scale properties (e.g., elastic constants, surface energies, vacancy migration energy) across a pool of 153 IPs from OpenKIM. A multi-linear regression model is built and validated to predict flow strength from small-scale predictors, with error bounds estimated via cross-validation. The model is then applied to DFT-computed predictors to estimate flow strength for seven FCC metals.

title: Advancing extrapolative predictions of material properties through learning to learn using extrapolative episodic training
research_summary: This study develops a meta-learning methodology—extrapolative episodic training (E2T)—to enhance machine learning models' ability to predict material properties beyond the distribution of training data. Using attention-based matching neural networks (MNNs) trained on arbitrarily generated extrapolative tasks, the approach demonstrates superior generalization for unseen material domains, validated on two case studies: predicting specific heat and refractive index of polymeric materials, and bandgap of hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites.

title: Probing out-of-distribution generalization in machine learning for materials
research_summary: This paper systematically evaluates the out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization capabilities of various machine learning models across over 700 OOD tasks derived from three large ab initio materials databases (JARVIS, Materials Project, OQMD). It challenges common heuristic definitions of OOD tasks (e.g., leave-one-element-out, leave-one-period-out, space group exclusion) by revealing that most such tasks are not truly extrapolative but rather represent interpolation within the high-dimensional materials representation space. Using UMAP-based domain identification and SHAP analysis, the study demonstrates that poor OOD performance is associated with test data lying outside the training domain in representation space, and crucially, that neural scaling laws (increasing training size/time) fail or even degrade performance on these representationally OOD tasks—contrary to expectations. The work calls for more rigorous, representationally grounded OOD benchmarks.

title: Known Unknowns: Out-of-Distribution Property Prediction in Materials and Molecules
research_summary: The paper proposes a transductive machine learning method—Bilinear Transduction—to improve zero-shot extrapolation for predicting out-of-distribution (OOD) property values of materials and molecules, i.e., property values beyond the range observed in training data. It targets compositionally driven variation in solids (using stoichiometry-based representations) and graph-based variation in molecules (using SMILES-derived RDKit descriptors), aiming to boost precision and recall of high-performing OOD candidates during virtual screening.

title: Dielectric tensor prediction for inorganic materials using latent information from preferred potential
research_summary: This study leverages multi-rank equivariant structural embeddings from a universal neural network potential to enhance predictions of dielectric tensors. We develop an equivariant readout decoder to predict total, electronic, and ionic dielectric tensors while preserving O(3) equivariance, and benchmark its performance against state-of-the-art algorithms. Virtual screening of thermodynamically stable materials from Materials Project for two discovery tasks, high-dielectric and highly anisotropic materials, identifies promising candidates including Cs2Ti(WO4)3 (band gap Eg = 2.93eV, dielectric constant ε = 180.90) and CsZrCuSe3 (anisotropic ratio αr = 121.89). The results demonstrate our model’s accuracy in predicting dielectric tensors and its potential for discovering novel dielectric materials.

title: A Space Group Symmetry Informed Network for O(3) Equivariant Crystal Tensor Prediction
research_summary: We consider the prediction of general tensor properties of crystalline materials, including dielectric, piezoelectric, and elastic tensors. A key challenge here is how to make the predictions satisfy the unique tensor equivariance to O(3) group and invariance to crystal space groups. To this end, we propose a General Materials Tensor Network (GMTNet), which is carefully designed to satisfy the required symmetries. To evaluate our method, we curate a dataset and establish evaluation metrics that are tailored to the intricacies of crystal tensor predictions. Experimental results show that our GMTNet not only achieves promising performance on crystal tensors of various orders but also generates predictions fully consistent with the intrinsic crystal symmetries.

title: COMPLETE AND EFFICIENT GRAPH TRANSFORMERS FOR CRYSTAL MATERIAL PROPERTY PREDICTION
research_summary: Crystal structures are characterized by atomic bases within a primitive unit cell that repeats along a regular lattice throughout 3D space. The periodic and infinite nature of crystals poses unique challenges for geometric graph representation learning. Specifically, constructing graphs that effectively capture the complete geometric information of crystals and handle chiral crystals remains an unsolved and challenging problem. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach that utilizes the periodic patterns of unit cells to establish the lattice-based representation for each atom, enabling efficient and expressive graph representations of crystals. Furthermore, we propose ComFormer, a SE(3) transformer designed specifically for crystalline materials. ComFormer includes two variants; namely, iComFormer that employs invariant geometric descriptors of Euclidean distances and angles, and eComFormer that utilizes equivariant vector representations. Experimental results demonstrate the state-of-the-art predictive accuracy of ComFormer variants on various tasks across three widely-used crystal benchmarks.

title: CRYSTALFORMER: INFINITELY CONNECTED ATTENTION FOR PERIODIC STRUCTURE ENCODING
research_summary: Predicting physical properties of materials from their crystal structures is a fundamental problem in materials science. In this work, we show that this infinitely connected attention can lead to a computationally tractable formulation, interpreted as neural potential summation, that performs infinite interatomic potential summations in a deeply learned feature space. We then propose a simple yet effective Transformer-based encoder architecture for crystal structures called Crystalformer.

title: A Diffusion-Based Pre-training Framework for Crystal Property Prediction
research_summary: The paper proposes CrysDiff, a diffusion-based pretrain-finetune framework to address the challenge of limited labeled data for crystal property prediction. In pre-training, it reconstructs crystal structures (lattice and fractional coordinates) from atom compositions using a joint denoising diffusion model with equivariant GNNs to respect crystal symmetries. In fine-tuning, it models the conditional distribution of target properties given crystal structures by diffusing on the property value while keeping the structure fixed. It demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on multiple properties in the JARVIS-DFT dataset, especially under sparse labeling.

title: Structure-aware graph neural network based deep transfer learning framework for enhanced predictive analytics on diverse materials datasets
research_summary: This paper presents a structure-aware graph neural network (GNN) based deep transfer learning framework to improve predictive performance for materials properties using sparse data. It leverages the ALIGNN architecture trained on large source datasets (e.g., Materials Project formation energy) and applies transfer learning—via fine-tuning or feature extraction—to small target datasets across diverse materials classes (3D/2D, inorganic/organic, computational/experimental) and properties. Evaluation across 115 dataset-property combinations shows transfer learning models outperform scratch-trained models in ≈90% of cases, with particular gains for small datasets and extrapolation tasks.

title: Higher-order equivariant neural networks for charge density prediction in materials
research_summary: We introduce ChargE3Net, an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network for predicting electron density in atomic systems. ChargE3Net enables the learning of higher-order equivariant features to achieve high predictive accuracy and model expressivity. We show that ChargE3Net exceeds the performance of prior work on diverse sets of molecules and materials. When trained on the massive dataset of over 100K materials in the Materials Project database, our model is able to capture the complexity and variability in the data, leading to a significant 26.7% reduction in self-consistent iterations when used to initialize DFT calculations on unseen materials. Furthermore, we show that non-self-consistent DFT calculations using our predicted charge densities yield near-DFT performance on electronic and thermodynamic property prediction at a fraction of the computational cost.

title: MD-HIT: Machine learning for material property prediction with dataset redundancy control
research_summary: This paper addresses the problem of overestimated machine learning model performance in materials science due to dataset redundancy—i.e., highly similar materials in training and test sets causing information leakage. It proposes MD-HIT, a redundancy reduction algorithm inspired by bioinformatics' CD-HIT, to generate non-redundant composition and structure datasets using distance metrics (e.g., Mendeleev, MatScholar, XRD, OFM). The authors apply MD-HIT to formation energy and band gap prediction tasks, demonstrating that models evaluated on redundancy-controlled datasets show lower (but more realistic) performance, especially for out-of-distribution samples, thus enabling objective evaluation of extrapolation capability.

title: Virtual Node Graph Neural Network for Full Phonon Prediction
research_summary: The paper introduces the Virtual Node Graph Neural Network (VGNN) to predict phonon spectra and bandstructures directly from atomic coordinates, addressing challenges of variable-length output and complex unit cells. It presents three variants—vector (VVN), matrix (MVN), and momentum-dependent matrix (k-MVN) virtual nodes—to predict Γ-point phonons and full phonon dispersion. The models are trained on ab initio DFPT phonon data and validated on diverse alloy systems; MVN is used to build a Γ-phonon database of 146,000+ Materials Project materials.

title: JARVIS-Leaderboard: a large scale benchmark of materials design methods
research_summary: Lack of rigorous reproducibility and validation are signiﬁcant hurdles for scientiﬁc development across many ﬁelds. Materials science, in particular, encompasses a variety of experimental and theoretical approaches that require careful benchmarking. Leaderboard efforts have been developed previously to mitigate these issues. However, a comprehensive comparison and benchmarking on an integrated platform with multiple data modalities with perfect and defect materials data is still lacking. This work introduces JARVIS-Leaderboard, an open-source and community-driven platform that facilitates benchmarking and enhances reproducibility.

title: Structure-based out-of-distribution (OOD) materials property prediction: a benchmark study
research_summary: This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark study evaluating graph neural networks (GNNs) for predicting materials properties on out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets—materials whose structures or properties deviate significantly from the training distribution. It introduces five OOD test set generation methods (LOCO, SparseXsingle, SparseYsingle, SparseXcluster, SparseYcluster) applied to three MatBench datasets (dielectric, elasticity, perovskites), and systematically compares eight SOTA GNN models across 250 folds. The study reveals a critical generalization gap: current top-performing GNNs underperform substantially on OOD tasks compared to their i.i.d. MatBench baselines, identifies CGCNN, ALIGNN, and DeeperGATGNN as comparatively robust, and analyzes latent physical spaces to explain performance differences.

title: A Recipe for Charge Density Prediction
research_summary: The paper proposes a machine learning method to predict quantum-mechanical charge density for atomic systems, aiming to overcome the accuracy–efficiency trade-off in existing approaches. It introduces three key ingredients: (1) representing charge density using atomic and virtual orbitals (spherical fields centered at atoms and bond midpoints), (2) using expressive, domain-informed, and learnable even-tempered Gaussian basis sets, and (3) employing a high-capacity equivariant neural network (eSCN). The method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while being >30× faster than prior methods on the QM9 charge density benchmark.

title: Learning Superconductivity from Ordered and Disordered Material Structures
research_summary: The paper introduces SuperCon3D, a new dataset containing both 3D crystal structures (ordered and disordered) and experimental superconducting transition temperatures (Tc), and proposes two deep learning models—SODNet for screening known structures and DiffCSP-SC for generating novel high-Tc superconductors. It validates both models via computational (e.g., DFT) and interpretability analyses, and reports candidate materials for experimental validation.
